title: Reading Drill — Comparing protective cases for maps — Reviewing the evidence
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Comparing protective cases for maps — Reviewing the evidence
passages.body:
**A** The map conservator in Brackenton received an old report about large maps rubbing against fasteners in storage. The report compared new abrasion marks, but some entries had been collected under different conditions. To check the report, reviewers returned to the condition photographs rather than treating the published figures as a complete record.

**B** The review covered eight weeks. In the first part of that period, the original records did not consistently include prior tears repaired with tape. In the later part, the recording sheet included a separate field for it. The reviewers kept readings from both periods, but marked which items were missing rather than guessing what had happened.

**C** The conclusion listed pockets with a clear margin as a possible later response. It recommended collecting another set of readings before deciding whether to use it. The new data would be published with the method, so another group could work out whether its own measurements were comparable.
